When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality. This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application. > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary). ## When to use Server and Client Components? The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case. Use **Client Components** when you need: - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). Here's the layout. The app is small, so there are only a few files that matter. ## Files | File | Role | |---|---| | `app/page.tsx` | The whole page. It is a Server Component with a hardcoded `PLANS` array. It holds the header, the Monthly/Annual toggle, the coupon input and Apply button, an empty `

` under the coupon for messages, and the grid of `PlanCard`s. | | `components/PlanCard.tsx` | Renders one plan. It also defines the `PlanView` type. Everything in it is a pre-formatted string (`"$19.00"`, `"$87.00"`) plus a `seats` number. The −/+ buttons and "Start free trial" have no handlers. | | `app/layout.tsx` | Root layout with Geist fonts and metadata. Nothing to change here. | | `app/globals.css` | Tailwind 4 theme tokens (`panel`, `line`, `chip`, `muted`, `accent`). | | `next.config.ts` | Turbopack with the Tailwind loader. It also enables `cacheComponents` and `partialPrefetching`. | The project is Next 16.4.6 and React 19.3. `AGENTS.md` says this Next differs from what I know, so I'll consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing any code. ## What's stubbed - **Billing period:** the Monthly/Annual buttons are static. The "on" style is hardcoded to Monthly. - **Coupon:** the input and Apply button do nothing. The empty `

` looks reserved for a status message like "Coupon applied" or "Invalid code". - **Seats:** the −/+ buttons do nothing. - **Totals:** `total` and `subtotal` are hardcoded strings. The card only shows a Subtotal line, so there's no slot yet for a volume discount or coupon discount. - **Pricing rules:** these exist only as feature bullets. Pro is $19 per seat for 1 to 50 seats. Team is $29 per seat for 3 to 50 seats, with 5% off at 10 or more seats. ## Where I'd put the pricing logic 1. **`lib/pricing.ts`, a pure module with no React.** It would hold: - the plan definitions as data (id, name, unit price, min and max seats, volume discount threshold and rate) - `calculateQuote({ plan, seats, period, coupon })`, which returns structured numbers: unit price, subtotal, volume discount, coupon discount, total - coupon validation - seat clamping to each plan's min and max This is the one place the rules live, and it's easy to unit test. I'd do the math in integer cents to avoid float errors, and only format to strings at the edge. 2. **A small client component for the interactive state**, probably `components/PricingTable.tsx` marked `"use client"`. It would own the billing period, coupon, and per-plan seat counts, and it would call `calculateQuote`. `app/page.tsx` can stay a Server Component that renders it. The toggle, coupon box and cards all share state, so they need to live under one client boundary. 3. **`PlanCard` stays presentational.** I'd change `PlanView` to carry the quote, or take a quote as a prop, and add `onSeatsChange` and a line for each discount. It would no longer receive pre-formatted strings. 4. **A server-side check, only if it matters.** Coupon validity usually shouldn't be decided in client code. If coupons are real, I'd add a Server Function that validates the code and re-runs `calculateQuote`, so the client can't make up a price. The docs show the pattern in `01-app/02-guides/interactive-apps.md`. If this is only a demo, a client-side lookup in `lib/pricing.ts` is fine. ## Questions before we build - What should the annual discount be, or is annual just 12 times monthly? - Does the 5% volume discount apply to Team only? - What coupon codes and rules do you want (percent or fixed, one-time or recurring)? - Is the coupon check client-only, or should the server be the source of truth? Once you've answered those, I'd start with `lib/pricing.ts` and its tests, then wire up the UI.

Nothing breaks, and no state ever goes out of range. This is from reading the code. I haven't clicked through it in a browser.

**Mashing minus on Team at 3 seats**
- The button is `disabled` whenever `quote.seats > minSeats` is false, so the browser ignores the clicks.
- If a click did get through, the handler is `setSeats((s) => clampSeats("team", s - 1))`, which clamps back to 3. That means the stored state can't drop below 3.
- The total stays at $87.00 and the seat count stays at 3.

**Mashing plus at 50**
- It's symmetric. The plus button is disabled at 50, and the handler clamps to 50 anyway. Team tops out at $1,450.00 and Pro at $950.00.

**Fast clicking in the middle of the range**
- The handlers use the functional form of `setSeats`, so rapid clicks each count and none are lost. Ten fast clicks from 3 land on 13.

**Rough edges**
- **Disabled buttons look clickable.** The `step` style has no `disabled:` variant, and `hover:bg-chip` still applies. At the limit the button looks normal and hovers normally, but does nothing. A `disabled:opacity-40 disabled:cursor-not-allowed` style would fix that.
- **Focus can drop.** If someone is tabbing through with the keyboard and the focused button becomes disabled, some browsers drop focus. It's minor, but keyboard users may notice.
- **No feedback about the limit.** Nothing says "minimum 3 seats" or "maximum 50" apart from the feature bullet.
- **No typed input.** Seats can only change with the buttons, so there's no other way to enter an out-of-range number. If you later add a typed field, `clampSeats` already handles non-finite and fractional input.

The coupon is wired up and the build and typecheck pass. I still haven't run either of your checks, because the shell wouldn't run the pricing code. I also haven't tried it in a browser. By hand, both of your numbers come out right.

**What changed**
- **`lib/pricing.ts`**:
  - `parseCoupon(input)` strips all whitespace and uppercases the input. It returns `"SAVE10"` or `null`, so `" save 10 "` is accepted.
  - `calculateQuote(planId, seats, coupon)` now returns `couponDiscountCents`. It is 10% of the subtotal, rounded to the nearest cent, and the total is the subtotal minus that discount.
- **`components/PricingTable.tsx`** (new, a client component): it owns the coupon input, the applied coupon and the message. The coupon is shared state, so it applies to both cards. Apply is a form submit, so pressing Enter in the box also works.
- **`components/PricingCard.tsx`**: it takes the applied coupon and passes it to the quote.
- **`components/PlanCard.tsx`**: when a coupon is applied, it shows a "Coupon (SAVE10): −$9.50" line under Subtotal.
- **`app/page.tsx`**: the static coupon box and cards are replaced by `PricingTable`.

**Messages**
- A valid code shows `SAVE10 applied: 10% off`.
- Anything else, including an empty box, shows `Invalid code`.

**Your checks by hand**
- Pro, 5 seats: 9500 − 950 = 8550, which is $85.50.
- Team, 3 seats: 8700 − 870 = 7830, which is $78.30.

To confirm in the browser, run `npm run dev`, type `save10` into the box and click Apply. Pro should show $19.00 at 1 seat and press + four times to reach $85.50. Team should show $78.30 at its starting 3 seats.

**Choices to flag**
- **A bad code removes an applied coupon.** If SAVE10 is applied and someone then applies garbage, they see "Invalid code" and the discount goes away. The alternative is to keep the old discount, which would show "Invalid code" next to a still-discounted price. Tell me if you'd prefer that.
- **Typing doesn't change the price.** The discount only takes effect when Apply is pressed, and the message stays until the next Apply.
- **Rounding is to the nearest cent.** It makes no difference for 10% of the current prices, but it will matter if other percentages or Team's volume discount come in.

The coupon logic is in one place, and nothing is duplicated, so I haven't changed anything.

**All the rules live in `lib/pricing.ts`**
- The code list and percentage are in `COUPONS` (`SAVE10: 10`).
- The case and whitespace normalisation is in `parseCoupon`.
- The discount math and rounding are in `calculateQuote`, at line 47.

**Both cards share one implementation.** Pro and Team are two instances of the same `PricingCard` component, which calls `calculateQuote(planId, seats, coupon)`. There's no per-plan coupon code. `PricingTable` holds the single applied coupon and passes it to both.

**What's left outside `lib/pricing.ts` is display only**
- `PricingTable.tsx:18` builds the message `SAVE10 applied: 10% off`. It reads the percentage from `COUPONS` rather than hardcoding it, so adding a coupon there updates the message.
- `PricingCard.tsx` and `PlanCard.tsx` format the quote into the `Discount (SAVE10): -$9.50` line.

If you want, I could move the "applied" and "Invalid code" message strings into `lib/pricing.ts` so every coupon-related string lives next to the rules. I held back because it mixes user-facing copy into the pricing module.
